The dust motes danced in the sliver of afternoon light that pierced the heavy velvet curtains, illuminating the silence that had fallen over the study. The antique clock on the mantel ticked with a rhythmic, mechanical indifference, each second a hammer blow against the fragile peace of the room. Adrian stood by the fireplace, his back rigid, facing the circle of faces that had once been his closest confidants. Now, they were accusers, their eyes sharp with the sting of betrayal, yet clouded by the dawning realization of his sacrifice.

"I may have made a mistake," Adrian began, his voice trembling not from fear, but from the weight of the truth he had carried alone. He looked at Sarah, then at Marcus, his gaze lingering on each of them. "But I did it to protect all of us."

The words hung in the air, heavy and suffocating. For a moment, no one moved. The betrayal was palpable, a cold draft in the warm room. But as the silence stretched, the anger began to fracture, giving way to a complex, aching understanding. They saw the exhaustion in his posture, the shadows under his eyes that spoke of sleepless nights spent shielding them from a danger they never knew existed. It was not just remorse he wore; it was a quiet, steadfast admiration for the bond that had survived the lie.

The priority question asks for the name of the amphibian that can change its color to blend with the environment.

The amphibian that can change its color to blend with the environment is the chameleon.
